verdict.text: The registry now logs in to SeaweedFS keylessly through its own role, and the live cutover evidence covers every part of r2.
The marker cleanup was guarded and checked against MinIO, and leaving the HAProxy jobspec comment stale follows the repo's rule and is recorded in the component page.
Pass.
Gates, re-run from the worktree with `loopctl gate stamp`: pre_commit pass, cli_tests pass, eval-row r1 pass, stamp green dabdea1236a1806a20377a424e310cac3dbc685b83b388b978326a3795c67e6b.
Code: registry.hcl identity is `seaweedfs` with audience `seaweedfs` and JWT at secrets/nomad_seaweedfs.jwt.
The helper POSTs to s3_host:8333 with RoleArn=arn:aws:iam::role/registry and RoleSessionName=registry.
regionendpoint is `http://s3_host:8333`.
services.tf passes s3_host from data.consul_service.seaweedfs, which exists in the root.
The registry role already exists in local.seaweedfs_keyless_jobs (infrastructure root) and grants s3:* on the bucket.
That covers the actions spike 1 named.
Dropping depends_on on minio_iam_policy.registry_wi is right because nothing in this root gates the role now.
The policy, the Vault KV entry and the static keys stay as rollback paths, as the comments say.
Escaping (`$${jwt}`) still matches the double-template rule.
r1: tests/test_registry_s3.py asserts each part of fails_when.

It checks the audience `seaweedfs` inside the identity block, RoleArn and RoleSessionName inside the STS URL, that 192.168.2.29:9000 is absent, and that regionendpoint uses s3_host fed by the Consul lookup.
Reverting any of these fails a test.
r2 (judgment): read spike 2's README, stdout.txt, run.json (exit 0) and the scripts.
backup-minio alloc e12ec616 and restore-s3 alloc 72fa47f2 both exited 0.
restore-s3 runs rclone check, so a 0 exit means the check passed.
snapshot.py compared all 33 tags by tag and digest, plus config hashes and 192 layer digests and sizes, against a baseline taken on MinIO before the switch.
Layers went through the presigned SeaweedFS redirect.
The result was identical.
push_check.py pushed a new OCI image (201) and read it back by tag and digest (200), and the layer bytes matched.
SeaweedFS went from 399 to 404 objects and MinIO stayed at 399.
That meets the outcome.
Marker deletion (drop_markers.py): it refuses if MinIO has any key ending in `/`, and it deletes only zero-byte `/` keys in SeaweedFS.
It then requires SeaweedFS's full key-to-size map to equal MinIO's, and MinIO was frozen because the registry was stopped.
The 725 matches the count predicted in spike:backup-durable-buckets/3.
The equality check after the delete also rules out SeaweedFS having deleted directory contents along with a marker.
This is sound, and gcs-backups.md records that a future registry restore needs the same step.
HAProxy step 3: the edge path did not change.
Only the backend behind the registry moved.
The comment that still says MinIO sits inside a jobspec, so editing it would re-register HAProxy.
.claude/rules/terraform-file-layout.md says a stale reference there stays stale, and container-registry.md says so next to the timeout trap.
Acceptable.
Docs: read the diff of every changed docs/ and .okf page.

Checked the claims that MinIO has no keyless job and only backup-minio reads it (memex.hcl is commented out), that 8333 is open to 192.168.0.0/16 (infrastructure/services.tf:360), and that default/registry/seaweedfs exists (applications/secrets.tf:476).
The frozen-backup gap is stated in the reference page, gcs-backups.md, minio.md and container-registry.md.
None.
The check image's five objects (repo seaweedfs-cutover-check, manifest deleted) stay in SeaweedFS until someone runs registry garbage-collect.
They do no harm.
push_check.py pushed small blobs with a single PUT, so this run did not exercise chunked or multipart pushes on the production job.
Spike 1 covered them with the same registry version and role credentials, so I accept it.
